newsitem.title: UK: European VGO falls with shut arb to the U.S.
newsitem.headline: European VGO falls with shut arb to the U.S.

text.p: European vacuum gas oil continued the weakness shown at the end of last week with a closed arb to the United States forcing material into Europe, traders said on Wednesday.
"VGO is very depressed at the moment," said a trader.
Traders said the netback price for moving low sulphur VGO to the United States was very low -- about $110 per tonne or even less for 50,000 tonne cargoes.
"The normal flow for VGO is to go transatlantic, but with falling crude prices the price of VGO in the States is also falling which makes the arbitrage closed," the trader said.
"This is pushing a lot of VGO on the European market which is pushing prices down," he added.

There was unconfirmed talk of a Northern European trader having sold its cargo but no further details were available. One trader said the seller was recently considering offers as low as $108 and $109.
At least two other traders were heard offering less distressed cargoes.
However, traders said the VGO barge market was looking a little better than cargoes.
"The cargo market is weak, and the barge market, is not healthy but it is moving and barge prices are fairly high," a second trader said.
A third trader said although overall levels were low VGO may recover "because the Russians are refusing to sell at these low prices."

Turkey's state oil refinery, Tupras, said on Wednesday that it awarded Dutch trader Vitol with its 30,000-tonne heavy vacuum gas oil export tender at a premium of plus $9.01 per tonne with shipment on June 20-25.
Tupras said it put out the tender on June 2.
